rules.sentence: Keratosis pilaris is a chronic condition most common in the adolescent population.
The condition characteristically presents with papules with follicular involvement and surrounding erythema typically located on the extensor surfaces of the proximal upper and lower extremities.
Keratosis pilaris first appears in early childhood and progresses, becoming most extensive during the second decade of life.
Keratosis pilaris is associated with many other conditions, including atopic dermatitis, ichthyosis vulgaris, obesity, diabetes mellitus, and malnutrition.
Emollients, exfoliants, antiinflammatory medications, phototherapy, and various laser therapies can treat keratosis pilaris.[2]
